chapter: Chicago boyhood and the Austin High Gang
title: Bix's tone and taste; copying the Wolverines' records
summary: He admires Bix's tone and harmonic choices and says the gang learned all the Wolverines numbers from their Gennett records.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: But Bix was, I liked the musical sound of his tone. And also his choice of notes, his taste, his harmony. A sixth or a ninth or a seventh, the way he would lay these little things in there. Which he would do unconsciously too. Because those were things that were in his head harmonically and they came out on the cornet.
But what happened was this. After, to carry on in the Bix Beiderbecke vein, we copied all the numbers
off the recordings that they had made and (Gennett) records and we knew every number that they had recorded and knew it in the right key.
